controlled_change: Resident versus exact packed embedding rows in one fixed-priming producer; 1460 target and 32 draft slots, 12GiB admission, widths four and one measured separately.
correctness: All six replacement numerical pairs match. Twelve cross-producer comparisons match proposals, all logits, state, boundaries and admission. Some numerical diagnostics compress; clean full-model correctness remains unqualified.
decision_origin: authored interpretation; original report statuses retained
expected_effect: Recover about 642MiB of planned memory for a separate expert cache experiment.
hypothesis: Exact streamed embedding rows reduce physical footprint without changing MTP arithmetic or materially adding latency.
limitations: One short coding workload; two pairs per width, no confidence bounds.
Memory savings are measured; a speed benefit from extra cache remains unmeasured.
Clean full-model correctness and long-context/sustained qualification are incomplete.
outcome: Eight clean timing processes, two alternating 64-token pairs per width. Peak saving 644-647MiB. Rows/resident geometric latency ratios: width four 1.000342685, width one 1.001659370. Latency is essentially flat; no speedup demonstrated.
smallest_experiment: Capture complete four/eight-token target-cache lifetimes with trace-off numerical controls. Reproduce native CLOCK before simulating 1909/2048 slots. Change no cache size until admission is proven.
